nodes.label: Latin sC- → Spanish esC- (Prothetic e-)
nodes.rationale: Vulgar Latin disallowed syllable-initial s+consonant, extended to word-initial position via prothetic e-; Spanish alone kept both e- and s- (cf. It. drops e-, Fr. drops s-)

nodes.label: Latin f- → Spanish (Silent) h-
nodes.rationale: Word-initial Latin f- became unpronounced-but-written Spanish h-; later restored in spelling-only for learned borrowings (habitante, heroísmo); one of the most distinctive features setting Spanish apart from Portuguese/Catalan/French/Italian

nodes.label: Stress-Conditioned Vowel Diphthongization (e→ie, o→ue, + 6 shifts)
nodes.rationale: Diphthong appears only when stress falls on the syllable, producing Spanish's stem-changing 'diphthong verb' class (tiempo vs. temporal; pienso vs. pensamos)

nodes.label: Stop-Consonant Lenition and Double-Consonant Simplification
nodes.rationale: Interior Latin stops (p,b,t,d,c,g) survived, voiced, or vanished; double consonants eliminated for b,d,f,g,p,s,t in native words, surviving only as cc/ll/mm/nn/rr

nodes.label: pl/fl/cl → ll and ct → ch Consonant Shifts
nodes.rationale: Produces learned/popular doublets from the same Latin root (reverso/revés, parábola/palabra)

nodes.label: Goths and Germanic Contact Layer (5th-8th c.)
nodes.rationale: Visigothic rule of Iberia left proper names more than vocabulary; two systematic patterns: Germanic h- dropped, Germanic w- surfaces as gu- since Latin [w] had vanished

nodes.label: Arabic/Andalusi Contact Layer (8th-15th c.)
nodes.rationale: Spanish frequently absorbed the Arabic definite article al- fused into the borrowed noun itself (algodón, azúcar), far greater Arabic influence than on any other Romance language

nodes.label: -cer Inceptive Verb Family (Latin -scere)
nodes.rationale: Latin inceptive -scere ('to begin to [verb]') produced Spanish -cer verbs; same source produces English -ish suffix via Old French (abolish, cherish, flourish)

nodes.label: Esclavo → Chao/Ciao Etymological Chain
nodes.rationale: Medieval Lat. sclavus ('Slav'/'slave', an ethnonym-turned-slur since so many enslaved people were Slavic) → Venetian schiavo ('your humble servant') shortened to ciao → Spanish chao, a farewell-only borrowing; surprising etymological link between 'slave' and an everyday greeting

nodes.label: Algodón — Fused Arabic Article Example
nodes.rationale: Sp. algodón (al-+root) vs. Fr. coton/It. cotone (no fused article) — systematic contrast pattern repeated in azúcar/sucre/zucchero

nodes.label: Albaricoque — Five-Hop Loanword Chain
nodes.rationale: Lat. persicum praecoquum → Gk. praikokion → Arabic al-barquq → Sp. albaricoque → Fr. abricot → Eng. 'apricot' — a five-hop chain through four languages

nodes.label: Florecer/Flourish — Shared Inceptive-Suffix Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Direct morphological cognate of English 'flourish' via Old French, both descending from Lat. florescere — a 'mechanism echo' showing the same derivational morpheme surfacing as a verb-class marker in two daughter traditions

nodes.label: Germanic w- → Spanish gu- Pattern (guardar, guerra, guiar)
nodes.rationale: Same mechanism produced English doublets guard/ward, guardian/warden, guarantee/warranty (Norman French kept [w], central French/Spanish used [gw])

nodes.label: Representative Sampling Prioritizing Derivational Mechanism
nodes.rationale: At 655 pages full extraction is infeasible and would duplicate dictionaries already in corpus; file prioritizes the sound-change rule and contact-layer story over the vocabulary itself, directly comparable to the Hungarian gyerek→dzserek convergent contact-sound-change finding
